hints: Focus on what Brønsted-Lowry theory is really about, proton donation and proton acceptance, not about salts or solvents.
Look at $\text{NH}_4^+$ turning into $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NH}_2^-$ turning into $\text{NH}_3$, one loses $\text{H}^+$ and the other gains it.
Ask yourself which of the three statements actually describes proton transfer, and which just state true but irrelevant facts.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Brønsted-Lowry definition**

Remember, a Brønsted-Lowry acid is a proton ($\text{H}^+$) donor and a base is a proton acceptor. To classify a reaction this way, we must find proton transfer.

$$\text{acid} \rightarrow \text{conjugate base} + \text{H}^+$$

**Spot the proton transfer in this reaction**

Look at the nitrogen species. $\text{NH}_4^+$ becomes $\text{NH}_3$ by losing $\text{H}^+$, so it is the acid. $\text{NH}_2^-$ becomes $\text{NH}_3$ by gaining $\text{H}^+$, so it is the base.

$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{NH}_2^- \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3$$

**Test each statement**

Statement 1 is true and directly explains the classification, it names the proton donor. Statement 2 is true that $\text{Na}^+\text{Cl}^-$ is a salt, but that does not prove proton transfer. Statement 3 is true that ammonia can be a nucleophile, but nucleophile describes attack on electron-deficient carbon, not Brønsted-Lowry behaviour here.

So only 1 explains why this is a Brønsted-Lowry acid-base reaction.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all explanations. While 1 is correct, 2 and 3 do not explain Brønsted-Lowry behaviour. Being a salt and being a nucleophile are true facts but are irrelevant to proton donation and acceptance.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 together explain it. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is a trap. $\text{Na}^+\text{Cl}^-$ is indeed a salt, but salt formation happens in many reaction types and does not prove proton transfer occurred.
options.C: Incorrect. This option claims 2 and 3 explain it but leaves out 1. Both 2 and 3 miss the point. Nucleophilic behaviour is about donating a lone pair to an electron-deficient atom, while Brønsted-Lowry behaviour is specifically about donating or accepting $\text{H}^+$. Neither 2 nor 3 describes that.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 explains the classification. $\text{NH}_4^+$ acts as a Brønsted-Lowry acid by donating a proton to $\text{NH}_2^-$, the base, to form two molecules of $\text{NH}_3$. The spectator ions $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ take no part in the proton transfer.
